label: Mark 5:1
text: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

variants.reading: the country of the Gerasenes (την χωραν των Γερασηνων)
variants.note: The fetched Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac article gives Mark 5:1 as 'the region of the Gerasenes' and adds 'Other textual variations include "Gadarenes" and "Gergesenes"'; the WEB text reads 'Gadarenes'.

label: Mark 5:2
text: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.

label: Mark 5:3
text: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,

label: Mark 5:4
text: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.

label: Mark 5:5
text: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.

label: Mark 5:6
text: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,

label: Mark 5:7
text: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”

label: Mark 5:8
text: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”

label: Mark 5:9
text: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

variants.reading: λεγιων ονομα μοι ('Legion is my name to me')
variants.note: Codex Alexandrinus, Washingtonianus, Koridethi, family 1, family 13 and the Byzantine text read λεγεων (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark, Mark 5:9).

label: Mark 5:10
text: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

label: Mark 5:11
text: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.

label: Mark 5:12
text: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”

label: Mark 5:13
text: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.

label: Mark 5:14
text: Those who fed them fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.

label: Mark 5:15
text: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.

label: Mark 5:16
text: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.

label: Mark 5:17
text: They began to beg him to depart from their region.

label: Mark 5:18
text: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.

label: Mark 5:19
text: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”

label: Mark 5:20
text: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.

label: Mark 5:21
text: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.

label: Mark 5:22
text: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet,

label: Mark 5:23
text: and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”

label: Mark 5:24
text: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.

label: Mark 5:25
text: A certain woman, who had an issue of blood for twelve years,

label: Mark 5:26
text: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,

label: Mark 5:27
text: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.

label: Mark 5:28
text: For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”

label: Mark 5:29
text: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

label: Mark 5:30
text: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”

label: Mark 5:31
text: His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

label: Mark 5:32
text: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.

label: Mark 5:33
text: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

label: Mark 5:34
text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”

label: Mark 5:35
text: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”

label: Mark 5:36
text: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”

label: Mark 5:37
text: He allowed no one to follow him, except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

label: Mark 5:38
text: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.

label: Mark 5:39
text: When he had entered in, he said to them, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”

label: Mark 5:40
text: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.

label: Mark 5:41
text: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”

label: Mark 5:42
text: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.

label: Mark 5:43
text: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.

label: Jairus
aka: Jaeiros (Greek), from the Hebrew name Yair

label: Mark 5:1 sets the exorcism in the country of the Gadarenes
statement: Mark 5:1 sets the event in the country of the Gadarenes (Gerasenes in the oldest manuscripts), on the far side of the Sea of Galilee.

label: One man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs
statement: A man with an unclean spirit came out of the tombs to meet Jesus - one man, where Matthew tells of two demoniacs.

label: The demoniac could not be bound and cut himself with stones
statement: Nobody could bind the demoniac any more, not even with chains; night and day among the tombs and in the mountains he cried out and cut himself with stones.

label: The man named the demons 'Legion, for we are many'
statement: Asked his name, the man answered 'My name is Legion, for we are many' - the Greek transliterates Latin legio, a Roman military unit.

label: About two thousand pigs rushed into the sea and were drowned
statement: The unclean spirits entered a herd of about two thousand pigs feeding on the mountainside, which rushed down the steep bank into the sea and were drowned.

label: The healed man proclaimed in the Decapolis
statement: The healed man went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.

label: Jairus, one of the rulers of the synagogue, begged for his dying daughter
statement: Jairus, one of the rulers (archisynagogoi) of the synagogue, fell at Jesus's feet and begged him to come and lay his hands on his little daughter, who was at the point of death.

label: The woman had spent all she had on many physicians and grew worse
statement: The woman with the twelve-year flow of blood had suffered much under many physicians, had spent all she had, and grew worse rather than better.

label: Only Peter, James and John followed into the house
statement: Jesus allowed no one to follow him into the synagogue ruler's house except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

label: 'Talitha cumi' - Aramaic words to the girl
statement: Taking the girl by the hand, Jesus said 'Talitha cumi', which Mark translates 'Little girl, I tell you, get up' - a transliterated Aramaic phrase.

label: The girl was twelve years old and rose and walked
statement: The girl rose up and walked immediately, for she was twelve years old.

title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: The Gospel of Mark ( Mark 5:1–20 ) provides the earliest accounts. Jesus goes across the sea into the "region of the Gerasenes".

title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (Land of the Gadarenes)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: Most texts dating from before Origen refer to the area as the Land of the Gadarenes, leading many to believe that the location's identification with Gergasa in later texts and popular imagination to be a later corruption.

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (Decapolis proclamation)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: The man whom Jesus heals is also specifically mentioned to be a Gentile in Mark's gospel, and he was commanded to proclaim the Gospel to the Gentile residents of the Decapolis following his exorcism.

label: Wikipedia: Legio X Fretensis
title: Legio X Fretensis
excerpt: Legio X Fretensis ("Tenth legion of the Strait") was a legion of the Imperial Roman army . It was founded by the young Gaius Octavius (later to become Augustus Caesar ) in 41/40 BC to fight during the period of civil war that started the dissolution of the Roman Republic .

label: Wikipedia: Raising of Jairus' daughter
title: Raising of Jairus' daughter
excerpt: a ruler (Mark: εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων "one of the synagogue rulers"; Luke: ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς "a ruler of a synagogue") of a Galilean synagogue called Jairus ( Greek : Ἰάειρος , Iaeiros , from the Hebrew name Yair )

label: Wikipedia: Raising of Jairus' daughter (the bleeding woman)
title: Raising of Jairus' daughter
excerpt: Mark and Luke inform the reader that all this time nobody could heal her, with Mark dramatically adding 'she had spent all she had on physicians to no avail' (Mark 5:25–26; Luke 8:43).

label: Wikipedia: Raising of Jairus' daughter (Talitha koum)
title: Raising of Jairus' daughter
excerpt: In Mark's account, the Aramaic phrase Talitha koum (transliterated into Greek as ταλιθα κουμ and reportedly meaning, "Little girl, I say to you, get up!") is attributed to Jesus (Mark 5:41 NIV).
